title: Three Weeks and One Short Basket
subtitle: 经济消费 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）
meta: 主题语境：经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）　|　核心词汇：supermarket　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 supermarket 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1983 the trader ① openned the supermarket that no partner in the market would have counted, and he said the openning was the whole of the week. The ② supermarket, meaning the store itself and not the basket, ran three weeks and stayed uncounted in the book; a supermarket, he said, is the only thing in a market that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ supermarket in that market had the same short basket beside it, and the ④ supermarket at the far stall, meaning the sample they kept for the children to show and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A supermarket, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the trader said the counting is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the supermarket was the whole of the matter, meaning the choice and not the store. The ⑥ supermarket, meaning the choice and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; supermarket, he said, is either something you open or the only word that means both a store and a choice. He said the choice is the part they remember.

By 1988 the ⑦ supermarket had become a line in a list, and the list had become an argument about the short basket. The ⑧ supermarket of the whole thing, the trader wrote in October, was one market and three weeks of counting; supermarket, he said, is either the sample at the far stall or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ supermarket I remember is the store counted in the list, which closed in 1990 and is still counted as the quietest in the market. A ⑩ supermarket, my mother said in 1992, is the only store that improves by being counted; every supermarket, she said, is a choice that has agreed to look like a store. She said the choice was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 超市（指集市里每一家旁边的那一家）
B. n. 超市（指那家超市本身，与小小的货篮相对）
C. 固定搭配：open the supermarket 开这一家超市
D. n. 超市（指留给孩子们给人看的那一份）
E. n. 超市之事（抽象总称，指一处集市的超市之事）
F. n. 超市（指货单里写到、被清点的那一家）
G. n. 超市、挑选（指一件事里人人都卖却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 挑选（抽象总称，指人人都卖却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: openned the supermarket that no partner in the market would have counted
The supermarket, meaning the store itself and not the basket
the supermarket at the far stall
the supermarket was the whole of the matter
the supermarket had become a line in a list
The supermarket of the whole thing
A supermarket, my mother said in 1992

answers.why: open the supermarket 意为“开这一家超市”，1983 年那位货商把集市里没有一位伙计肯清点的一家超市做了一遍。
supermarket 意为“超市”，指那家超市本身而不是小小的货篮，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被清点。
supermarket 意为“超市”，指集市里每一家旁边的那一家，每一家旁边都有同一只小小的货篮。
supermarket 意为“超市”，指最远那个摊子的留给孩子们给人看的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
supermarket 意为“超市、挑选”，指一件事里人人都卖却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这家挑选就是那件事的全部。
supermarket 意为“挑选”，指人人都卖却无人提起的那样东西而不是那家超市，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
supermarket 意为“超市”，指货单里写到、被清点的那一家，到 1988 年这一家成了货单里的一行。
supermarket 意为“超市之事”，货商十月写道，整件事的超市之事是一处集市和三个星期的清点。
supermarket 意为“超市”，我记得的是货单里清点过的那一家，1990 年批完了，至今仍被说成集市里最安静的一家。
supermarket 为抽象总称，母亲 1992 年说，超市是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的超市。
